newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea offers nine state industries for sale.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea offers nine state industries for sale.

text.p: The Eritrean government has invited bids for nine government industries -- including the profitable Asmara brewery -- under its privatisation programme.
The government said on Saturday that all bids for the Asmara Brewery, one of the country's most profitable industries, have to be submitted by September 15.
In 1996, it made a 30 million Birr ($4.38 million) gross profit, its acting manager Stifanos Habtemariam told Reuters.
This is the second batch of nine government industries put up for sale in a programme launched in March.
The first round covered oxygen, woodworks and plastics, furniture, soap, wine, dairy, shoe and cigarette industries.
The second batch includes the Asmara Brewery, textile factories, agro-industry, shoe factory, bus assembly, and a carton factory.
For the remaining eight industries, the closing date for bidding is August 29.
Last year the Eritrean government said it would sell 39 of its major industries.
The Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF), which fought a long guerrilla war for independence from neighbouring Ethiopia, formerly had a strong Marxist ideology.

Since independence in 1993, however, the ruling party, now renamed the People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), has said it wants to let privatised industries lead the country's economic growth.
